marginalia.note: Mellis viribus reficiendis accommodatissimum, praeter experientiam grauissimi autores prodiderunt, cumprimis vero fenibus & pituitosis naturis faluberrime esse, calidioribus vero, adolescentibus, aetateque florentibus & biliosis non aeque conuenit, facile enim iis in bilem vertitur. Gal. 2. de nat. facult. ex sententia Hipp. Unde Galenus in febribus hecticis à mellis vsu abstinendum fuadet l. 10. de morbis cur. propterea quod protinus vertatur in bilem, & ficciores acriorisque caloris reddat febres. Plin. l. 11. c. 12. 13. & seq. multa de melle scitu digna prodidit. Et l. 22. ca. 24. inquit, mellis natura talis est ut putrefactere corpora non finat, iucundo sapore atque non asperio, alia quam salis natura. Faucibus, tonsillis, anginae, omnibusque oris defideriis utilissimum, arefcentiq; in febrib. linguae &c. Haec Plin.

page.notes: Transcription is partly uncertain: the page is a slightly skewed scan with bleed-through from the facing page and the right margin is cropped. Marginal notes were placed in the left margin and attached to the paragraph where they stand; the note text is set in small italic type and some words are doubtful, so [?] markers are not applied throughout. The right-hand text is cut off at the scan edge, and the last line ends mid-word ("hom-"). The Greek word τεοφιμόν (θεοφιλόν / ἑκηφιλόν) is uncertain and copied as the best reading. The left-margin notes are read as close as the scan allows, but a careful check against the original is recommended before use.
